RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 50

An all-male panel is not proof of discrimination on its own, but it creates a recognized risk of affinity bias, especially in leadership hiring. However, the successful candidate's formal management training and broader leadership experience could be legitimate, non-discriminatory differentiators for a department-head role over specialized clinical qualifications.

Raising gender bias directly now—especially before receiving written feedback—can seem accusatory and damage professional relationships. Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting the delayed feedback and objective scoring criteria. If your institution has an explicit policy requiring diverse interview panels, you may neutrally inquire about adherence to panel composition standards, or consult HR or an employment advisor before deciding whether to escalate.
